claims.text: 5th Avenue & Spring Street had 153 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $10.5 million a year.
22% of crashes here were recorded as “angles” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
22% of crashes here were recorded as “entering at angle” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
2% of crashes here were recorded as “same direction -- both turning right -- both moving -- sideswipe” crashes, against 1% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 4.6 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.6 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Lighting would avoid about 3.1 crashes a year (CMF 7774, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.1 million a year; check on site: the corner has no street lighting now.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 5th Avenue, Seneca Street, Spring Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
